sources: Official Google Play Console Help, Android developer, App Store Connect Help and Apple Developer documentation, read 2026-11-20. Menu paths are quoted as of that day and the consoles change them: a launch pass confirms them in the live console. Fix a row once in flume and every PM inherits it.

requirements.title: Play Console developer account exists, fee paid, Developer Distribution Agreement accepted
requirements.why: Nothing can be published without a Play Console developer account; sign-up is a one-time US$25 fee plus legal acceptance and requires the account holder to be 18+.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console/signup while signed in to the Google Account that will own the app.
Review and accept the Developer Distribution Agreement.
Pay the one-time US$25 registration fee with a non-prepaid card (Mastercard, Visa, American Express, Discover US-only, Visa Electron non-US).
Choose the account type (personal or organization) and complete identity verification (see gp.identity-verification).
requirements.verify: Agent: Play Developer API call with the service account (for example edits.insert on the package) returns 200 instead of 401/403 once the account and app exist; or the owner's Play Console home lists the developer account.

requirements.title: Organization account D-U-N-S number (organization accounts only)
requirements.applies_when: organization account (mandatory for financial, health, VpnService and government apps)
requirements.why: An organization developer account cannot be created without a valid D-U-N-S number; the legal name and address in the Google payments profile must exactly match the Dun & Bradstreet record or the account risks restrictions and app removal.
owner_steps: Check for an existing D-U-N-S number or apply (free; can take up to 30 days) at https://www.dnb.com/duns/get-a-duns.html (Google warns against paid third-party D-U-N-S services).
In Play Console sign-up choose Organization and enter the D-U-N-S number when asked (it is read into the Google payments profile).
Make the payments profile legal name and address match the Dun & Bradstreet profile exactly; fix mismatches before any Google deadline.
requirements.verify: Agent cannot see the payments profile. Owner confirms in Play Console > Settings > Developer account (path quoted from Android developer verification guide: 'Settings page ... Developer Account'). Not applicable if the account is personal.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to personal accounts. Known government bodies and regions Dun & Bradstreet does not cover can ask Google Play support for an alternative.

requirements.title: Developer identity verification (government ID, address, OTP-verified contact email, contact phone, developer email)
requirements.why: Identity verification must be completed before publishing; if Google cannot verify, the developer presence and apps may be removed and cannot be republished until verified. Personal accounts submit a government photo ID and proof of address (US); documents must exactly match the Google payments profile.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console and complete every verification task on the Home page (ID document, address, contact details).
Use a valid, unexpired, colour, well-lit original government ID whose name and address match the Google payments profile exactly; update the payments profile in the same task if there is a mismatch.

Verify contact email, contact phone and developer email with the one-time passwords Google sends. Identity and (personal accounts) device verification must be finished before the developer phone / contact phone can be verified.
Required documents differ by country; the US list is at https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/15633622.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the Home page shows no outstanding verification tasks. Agent has no API for this.

requirements.title: Verify access to a real Android device via the Play Console mobile app
requirements.applies_when: personal account created after Google's device-verification rollout (new personal accounts)
requirements.why: New personal-account developers must verify they have a non-rooted physical Android 10+ device with the Play Console mobile app before they can make an app available on Google Play.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console on the web as the account owner and go to Home.
Find the task 'Verify that you have access to an Android mobile device' and click View details.
Scan the QR code to install or open the Play Console mobile app on a physical, non-rooted Android 10+ device.
In the app, sign in as the account owner, select the developer account, tap Verify and follow the prompts (under a minute; the phone number is not collected).
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the Home task disappears. Agent cannot verify.
requirements.caveat: The exact account-creation cutoff for device verification is on https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14316361 (listed in search results, not fetched).

requirements.title: Declare EEA/UK trader or non-trader status for the account
requirements.why: Google requires every developer account to declare trader status under EEA/UK law; missing the deadline can block app updates and remove apps globally. Traders also self-certify legal compliance, add a terms-of-service link per app and (personal accounts) a public phone number and address.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, then Manage account > Account details > About you (path quoted from the Trader status declaration help page) and follow the prompts to declare trader or non-trader. A hobbyist with no commercial intent who does not distribute in the EEA/UK may declare non-trader; paid apps, in-app purchases or ads point to trader. Consult a legal professional if unsure.
If trader: select the app, go to Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content and confirm trader status for that app; add the app's terms-of-service link and self-certify.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the declaration shows as complete under Manage account > Account details > About you.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content. Deadline 2027-02-01 is for existing accounts; the 2026-10-29 policy announcement also says declaration is required starting November 2026. Scope: Every active developer account; new accounts at creation, existing accounts by 2027-02-01.

requirements.title: Payments profile, bank account and merchant tax information for selling
requirements.applies_when: app is paid or sells in-app products/subscriptions
requirements.why: Selling anything on Google Play requires a Google payments profile with legal business info, a bank account registered in the payments profile country, and tax information; bank verification can take up to five days. A free app cannot later become paid.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, then Manage account > Play apps settings > Monetization settings > Payments profile (path quoted from the Payments profile help page; the same page notes the older 'Setup > Payments profile' route).
Click Create payments profile, enter legal name, legal address (no PO boxes), primary contact and public business information, then Submit.
Add and verify a bank account (deposit challenge or bank documents, up to five days) and enter merchant tax information per https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10463498.
requirements.verify: Agent with a Play Developer API service account can read in-app products (inappproducts.list / monetization.onetimeproducts.list) once monetization is enabled; a 403 on those calls suggests the profile is not set up. Owner confirms the payments profile page status.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to a permanently free app with no in-app products. Japan: the 2026-10-29 announcement says anyone selling into or out of Japan must finish authorisation by 2026-12-01 or payments are held globally.

requirements.title: Android developer verification: package name registered to the account (and signing-key ownership proven if prompted)
requirements.why: Android developer verification takes effect 2026-09-30 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on certified devices and expands globally in 2027; Play developers must register their package names. For apps created in Play Console the registration is automatic.
requirements.agent_path: Developer APIs for verification launched in August 2026 (see https://developer.android.com/developer-verification); not read in detail. Agent can check the package name and signing certificate it uploads match the Play-registered app via the Play Developer API (edits.apks/bundles upload succeeds) and via bundletool.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console and look at the Home page for any package-name registration warning (quoted guidance: 'you should check your Play Console Home page').
If prompted, follow the on-screen prompt to prove ownership of the private signing key for the package.
Confirm the account identity under Settings > Developer account.
requirements.verify: Agent: after the first AAB upload, the app exists in the account so Play auto-registers the package name; owner confirms no registration warning on the Home page.
requirements.caveat: Owner steps are only needed if the Home page shows a warning; for new apps created in Play Console Google registers the package automatically. Scope: Distribution on Google Play.

requirements.title: Create the app in Play Console (permanent package name, free/paid choice, policy and export declarations, Play App Signing terms)
requirements.why: The app record is the container for every other requirement; the package name is permanent and cannot be deleted or reused, and the free/paid choice cannot go from free to paid later.
requirements.agent_path: None: the Play Developer API reference has no create-app method (every endpoint needs an existing package name).
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console and click Create app.
Enter the app name, default language, App or Game, Free or Paid (a free app cannot be made paid later), and the contact email for users.
Tick the Developer Program Policies declaration, the US export laws declaration and accept the Play App Signing Terms of Service.
Click Create app.
requirements.verify: Agent: a Play Developer API call with the package name (for example edits.insert then edits.get) succeeds only if the app exists.

requirements.title: Release targets Android 16 (API level 36) or higher
requirements.why: Since 2026-08-31 new apps and updates must target API 36; the 2026-11-01 extension window has passed.
requirements.agent_path: Inspect the built AAB with bundletool (bundletool dump manifest --bundle=app.aab | grep targetSdkVersion) or aapt2; the Play Developer API edits.bundles.upload / edits.commit also rejects non-compliant uploads.
requirements.verify: Agent: targetSdkVersion in the AAB manifest is >= 36; Play Console Policy status shows no target-API violation.
requirements.caveat: Scope: Phones/tablets; Wear OS/Automotive: API 35; TV/XR: API 34.

requirements.title: Upload a signed Android App Bundle (.aab) with an increasing versionCode
requirements.why: Google Play builds the delivered APKs from an app bundle; versionCode must rise with each upload and cannot exceed 2100000000.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API edits.bundles.upload then edits.tracks.update/patch then edits.commit (service account with release permission).
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.bundles.list shows the uploaded versionCode; edits.tracks.get shows it on the intended track.
requirements.caveat: Scope: APKs are only allowed for apps created before August 2021. The Play App Signing page does not say new apps must use an AAB; the release page says only apps created before August 2021 may use APKs. Ship an AAB.

requirements.title: Play App Signing enrolled and an upload key registered
requirements.why: New apps are enrolled in Play App Signing when created or on first bundle upload; Google keeps the app signing key and the developer signs bundles with a separate upload key.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API appsigning.enrollApp / rotateAppSigningKey exist; the upload keystore stays with the agent's secret store (never in the repo).
owner_steps: Console path per the Play App Signing help page today: Protected with Play > Play Store protection > Manage Play app signing (the page does not mention the older 'Test and release > App integrity').
requirements.verify: Agent: the first AAB upload is accepted and signed by the upload key; Manage Play app signing in the console shows the key fingerprints.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content. The signing page gives "Protected with Play > Play Store protection > Manage Play app signing", not "Test and release > App integrity".

requirements.title: Native code supports 16 KB memory page sizes
requirements.applies_when: app contains native code (.so libraries, C/C++, Godot/Unity/Unreal engines)
requirements.why: Apps targeting Android 15+ must support 16 KB page sizes on 64-bit devices; per developer.android.com, from 2027-02-01 updates that do not support it cannot be released. The Play technical-quality page lists it as a bundle requirement with no date.
requirements.agent_path: Run check_elf_alignment.sh <apk> (all arm64-v8a libs must say ALIGNED), zipalign -c -P 16 -v 4 <apk>, and llvm-objdump -p lib.so | grep LOAD (align must be 2**14); AGP >= 8.5.1 and NDK r28+ build aligned by default.
requirements.verify: Agent: ELF LOAD segment alignment >= 2**14 for every arm64-v8a/x86_64 .so and zipalign 16 KB check passes on the release artifact; bundletool dump config shows PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K.
requirements.caveat: Date discrepancy: developer.android.com says 2027-02-01; the Play Console quality page (answer 17492799) gives no date for mobile. Treat as required now.

requirements.title: Native code ships 64-bit libraries
requirements.why: The Play technical-quality page says apps with native code must support 64-bit-only architectures.
requirements.agent_path: Inspect lib/ folders in the AAB (unzip -l app.aab | grep '\.so$') for arm64-v8a (and x86_64).
requirements.verify: Agent: arm64-v8a libraries present for every native library.

requirements.title: Google Play Billing Library version still supported (v8+)
requirements.applies_when: app sells digital goods or subscriptions through Google Play Billing
requirements.why: Billing Library 7 hit its new-app/update deadline on 2026-08-31 (extension to 2026-11-01 has passed); use version 8 or newer. Digital goods on Play must use Google Play Billing.
requirements.agent_path: Check the app's build.gradle / merged manifest for com.google.android.play.billingclient.version >= 8.
requirements.verify: Agent: the merged manifest meta-data com.google.android.play.billingclient.version >= 8.x and Play Console Policy status shows no billing deprecation warning.

requirements.title: Closed test: at least 12 testers opted in continuously for 14 days
requirements.why: Until met, the Production and Pre-registration tracks stay disabled. A tester who leaves before 14 days does not count; leaving and rejoining needs consecutive 14 days.
requirements.agent_path: Agent can upload the AAB to a closed track and manage the tester list: Play Developer API edits.tracks.update on the closed track and edits.testers (Google Groups). Opt-in counts are shown in the console; the API reference read does not list an opt-in counter.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, then Test and release > Testing > Closed testing (path from the Closed testing help page).
Click Create track (or Manage track), open the Testers tab, add testers by Create email list or Google Groups, add a feedback URL/email, copy the opt-in link and Save changes.

Create and roll out a release to the closed track (upload the AAB, set release notes, Start rollout). The opt-in link only appears once the app status is Published, and can take several hours after first publish.

Send the opt-in link to at least 12 testers; each must actively opt in (being on a list is not enough) and stay opted in for 14 consecutive days. Testers who opted into the internal test must opt out of it first.
Optional: watch feedback under Monitor and improve > Ratings and reviews > Testing feedback.
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.tracks.get for the closed track shows a release in 'completed' status; day-count and opted-in tester count are visible to the owner on the Play Console Dashboard (Apply for production becomes available). Agent should track the start date in its ticket and compare to today.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to personal accounts created before 2023-11-13 or to organization accounts. No Play Developer API field for opted-in testers was seen: the agent tracks the closed-test start date itself and reads the tester count from the console Dashboard.

requirements.title: Apply for production access and be approved
requirements.applies_when: personal developer account created after 2023-11-13 (after the closed test is complete)
requirements.why: Google reviews the application (usually seven days or less) before Production and Open testing unlock; the account owner receives the result by email.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, and open the Dashboard.
Click Apply for production.
Section 1 'About your closed test': how easy recruiting was, how engaged testers were, summary of feedback and how you gathered it. Click Next.
Section 2 'About your app/game': target audience, value proposition, expected first-year installs. Click Next.
Section 3 'About your production readiness': changes made from testing and how you decided it is ready. Click Apply (answers are not saved if you leave before Next/Apply).
Wait for the email to the account owner; Google may ask you to keep testing if you had fewer than 12 opted-in testers or low engagement.
requirements.verify: Agent: Test and release > Production becoming enabled; API edits.tracks.update on the production track stops failing with a production-access error.

requirements.title: Privacy policy URL on the store listing and in the app
requirements.why: A publicly reachable privacy policy (https, valid certificate, no login, not a PDF, specific to the app) is required before the Data safety form can be completed.
requirements.agent_path: Agent hosts the page (for example under the repo's site) and curl-verifies status 200 and HTTPS; entering the URL in the console has no API.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content (path quoted from the help page today).
Under 'Privacy Policy' choose Start declaration (or Manage), type the policy URL and save.
requirements.verify: Agent: curl -sI <policy URL> returns 200 over valid TLS from outside the network; the policy text covers collection, use, sharing and deletion. Owner confirms the App content page row shows complete.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content. Scope: Even if no personal data is collected.

requirements.title: Data safety form completed and accurate
requirements.why: Every app on a test or production track must have a completed Data safety section matching real behaviour including SDK data; misrepresentation can block updates or remove the app.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API applications.dataSafety: POST https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com/androidpublisher/v3/applications/{packageName}/dataSafety writes the safety labels (CSV import/export also exists in the console).
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content and under 'Data safety' choose Start.

Read the overview, Next; answer 'Data collection and security' (collected/shared, encrypted in transit, deletion request), pick data types (including SDKs and libraries), answer usage and handling per type, review the preview and Submit.
requirements.verify: Agent: App content shows a green check for Data safety; the declared types match an audit of the app's SDKs and network calls.
requirements.caveat: Owner steps are only needed if the agent cannot use the API path. Scope: Even apps that collect no data.

requirements.title: IARC content rating questionnaire submitted
requirements.why: New apps must complete the content-rating questionnaire; ratings are used to block or filter content and inaccurate answers can remove the app.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Policy > App content (path quoted from the Content ratings help page; other pages say Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content).
Under Content rating click Start, enter an email address for IARC correspondence, choose a category (game vs app) and click Next.
Answer every question, review the calculated ratings on the Summary page and click Submit.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms Content rating shows a rating on the App content page. Agent can pre-answer the questions in a ticket from the game's actual content.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content. Play Console menu labels disagree across Help pages (Policy > App content, or Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content): confirm in the live console.

requirements.title: Target audience and content declared
requirements.why: Declares age groups and drives Families Policy; the store listing must not use child-appealing marketing if the app is not child-directed. Requires ads declaration, app access and privacy policy to be done first.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Policy > App content > Target audience and content > Start (or Manage).
Pick the target age groups (choose several only if truly designed for each), answer the app-details and ads follow-ups, review the summary and click Save.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the row is complete on the App content page.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content.

requirements.title: Families Policy requirements (child-safe ad SDKs, neutral age screen, children's data rules)
requirements.applies_when: target audience includes children (ages under 13, or under 18 in some locales)
requirements.why: Apps whose target ages include children must use only Families Self-Certified Ads SDKs and follow Families Policy; mixed audiences need a neutral age screen.
requirements.agent_path: Agent audits SDK list against the Families Self-Certified Ads SDK list and checks the app for a neutral age screen.
requirements.verify: Agent: no non-certified ad SDK or AD_ID request in a children-targeted build; Target audience declared consistently with the listing.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable if the declared audience is adults/13+ only and the listing has no child-appealing marketing.

requirements.title: Ads declaration (contains ads yes/no)
requirements.why: The declaration drives the 'Contains ads' label; misrepresenting ad presence can suspend the app.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content.
In the 'Ads' section click Start declaration (or Manage), choose Yes or No after reading the Ads policy, and save.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the Ads row is complete; agent verifies the build contains or lacks ad SDKs consistent with the answer.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content.

requirements.title: App access (sign-in) instructions for reviewers
requirements.why: Reviewers must be able to reach all functionality; credentials must be reusable, valid from anywhere, in English, and bypass 2FA/OTP.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content.

In 'Sign-in details' click Start declaration (or Manage), then + Add new instructions and enter the demo credentials or steps (up to five sets); put OTP/MFA workarounds in 'Any other instructions'; save.
requirements.verify: Agent: the demo account in the instructions actually logs in against the production backend from a clean install.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content. Scope: Declare all functionality available, or provide credentials/instructions when any part is gated by login, membership, paywall or location. Play Console menu labels disagree across Help pages (Policy > App content, or Monitor and improve > Policy and programs > App content): confirm in the live console.

requirements.title: Account deletion: in-app path plus a public web deletion page, declared in Data safety
requirements.applies_when: app lets users create an account (in the app or via an external flow)
requirements.why: Apps with account creation must offer in-app deletion and a web link usable without the app; the URL is entered in the Data safety deletion questions and the page must load, name the app/developer and let users request deletion.
requirements.agent_path: Agent builds the in-app deletion flow and web page; curl-verifies the URL; data safety deletion fields can be set through the dataSafety API.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content > Data safety and answer the Data deletion questions, entering the web deletion URL.
requirements.verify: Agent: the web deletion URL returns 200, names the app/developer and exposes a request mechanism; in-app Settings has a prominent delete-account action that removes the account and associated data.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to apps with no accounts (for example local-only play).

requirements.title: Financial features declaration
requirements.why: Every developer with a published app must complete it, even with no financial features.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content (Policy and programs > App content).
In 'Financial features' select Start, choose 'My app doesn't provide any financial features', click Next, then Save.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the row is complete on App content / Policy status.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content. Scope: Apps with no financial features must still certify that.

requirements.title: Health apps declaration
requirements.why: The Health apps declaration form must be completed by all developers per Play Console Help; categories include activity and fitness, period tracking, medical device apps and human-subjects research.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content and complete the 'Health apps' declaration (choose the option that the app has no health features if true). Quote from help page today: path not stated in the page read; see https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14738291.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the row is complete on App content.
requirements.caveat: Only the search summary of this page was read, not the full article; exact steps unverified. Scope: All apps, even with no health features.

requirements.title: Government apps declaration
requirements.why: The Government apps declaration has been required on the App content page since 2023-01-31.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content and complete the 'Government apps' declaration. Only the search summary of this page was read; exact steps are on https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9514050.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the row is complete on App content.
requirements.caveat: Only the search summary of this page was read. Scope: Declare the app is not a government app.

requirements.title: Advertising ID declaration
requirements.why: Listed among the App content declarations; the Android advertising ID may only be used for advertising and user analytics.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content and complete 'Advertising ID' (Start). Exact page steps not fetched.
requirements.verify: Agent: merged manifest contains or omits com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID consistently with the declaration.
requirements.caveat: Policy page read describes the Ads policy, not the declaration steps; the declaration is named in the Prepare-your-app-for-review search result. Verify steps in console. Scope: Declare whether the app uses the advertising ID; apps solely targeting children must not request AD_ID at API 33+.

requirements.title: Permission declaration forms for sensitive permissions
requirements.applies_when: app requests sensitive permissions (SMS, call log, background location, all-files access, photo/video, fine location for API 37+, local network for API 37+, manage contacts)
requirements.why: Apps requesting sensitive permissions may need a declaration form before the release can be published; the 2026-10-29 announcement adds local-network, manage-contacts and fine-location declarations.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content and complete each permission declaration listed there; if a release errors on a permission, follow the link in the Preview and confirm screen.
requirements.verify: Agent: list requested permissions from the merged manifest; none sensitive means not applicable.
requirements.caveat: Conditional; most games request none. Location permission declarations become mandatory 2027-01-27; fine location needs a declaration only for API 37+ (not a targetSdk 36 build).

requirements.title: News and magazine app self-declaration
requirements.applies_when: app is a news or magazine app
requirements.why: All News & Magazine apps must declare themselves in Play Console.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to App content and complete the News apps declaration.
requirements.verify: Agent: not applicable unless the app is a news/magazine app.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to games.

requirements.title: Store listing text: app name (30), short description (80), full description (4000)
requirements.why: Title, short description and full description are required to publish; repetitive or irrelevant keywords can cause suspension.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API edits.listings.update/patch per language, then edits.commit.
owner_steps: Console path from the help page today: Grow users > Store presence > Store listings (or Main store listing).
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.listings.get returns title <=30, shortDescription <=80, fullDescription <=4000 for the default language.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content.

requirements.title: App icon 512x512 32-bit PNG with alpha, up to 1024 KB
requirements.why: The Play icon is required to publish and must not carry badges or text implying ranking, price or categories.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API edits.images.upload with imageType icon.
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.images.list(imageType=icon) returns an image; file is 512x512 PNG <=1024 KB.

requirements.title: Feature graphic 1024x500 JPEG or 24-bit PNG, no alpha
requirements.why: The feature graphic is required to publish.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API edits.images.upload with imageType featureGraphic.
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.images.list(imageType=featureGraphic) returns an image of 1024x500 without alpha.

requirements.title: Phone screenshots (2 to 8; JPEG/24-bit PNG, 320-3840 px per side, long side at most 2.3x short side, up to 8 MB)
requirements.why: At least two screenshots across device types are required to publish; 4+ at 1080 px or larger are recommended for promotional eligibility.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API edits.images.upload with imageType phoneScreenshots (and sevenInchScreenshots/tenInchScreenshots if targeted).
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.images.list(imageType=phoneScreenshots) returns 2-8 images in valid size/ratio.
requirements.caveat: The help page lists tablet minimums (4) under the same heading as promotion eligibility; confirm in console whether tablet shots are required for your device targeting. Scope: Tablet/Chromebook/foldable/Wear/TV/XR sets only if targeting those form factors.

requirements.title: Category, tags and contact email (phone/website optional) set
requirements.why: Category, tags and a contact email are part of the mandatory store settings; a website is recommended.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API edits.details.update (contactEmail, contactWebsite, defaultLanguage) for contact info; category is set in the console.
owner_steps: Console path from the help page: Store settings then 'Contact Details'; category under Grow users > Store presence > Store listings.
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.details.get returns contactEmail.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content.

requirements.title: Pricing and distribution: free vs paid and countries/regions
requirements.why: Free/paid is permanent in one direction (free apps cannot become paid); the first production rollout publishes to the chosen countries or regions.
requirements.agent_path: Agent can read country availability (edits.countryavailability.get); price changes for paid apps are console-only per the reference read.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Products > App pricing (path from the Set up your app's prices help page) and confirm Free/Paid; choose countries/regions on the production release.
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.countryavailability.get lists the intended countries.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited Play Console Help page as read on 2026-11-20; Play Console menus change and different Help pages show different labels for App content.

requirements.title: Create and roll out the production release; send changes for review
requirements.why: A launch on Google Play means rolling out a release to the production track; changes needing review go through Publishing overview and Send for review. Managed publishing cannot be used for the first publication; reviews can take from a few hours to seven days or longer.
requirements.agent_path: Play Developer API: edits.bundles.upload, edits.tracks.update (production release, status completed), edits.validate then edits.commit; the owner (or an owner-delegated service account) clicks final send. Commit fails while declarations are incomplete.
owner_steps: Open https://play.google.com/console, choose the app, go to Test and release > Production and click Create new release (top right).
Upload the AAB (or Add from library), name the release, and enter release notes per language wrapped in tags such as <en-US>...</en-US> (500 characters each); click Next.
On 'Preview and confirm' fix every error (warnings do not block), then click Save (or Publish if offered).
Open Publishing overview in the main menu and click Send for review under 'Changes not yet sent for review'; critical pre-review-check issues must be fixed first.
For a first release there is no rollout percentage: click Start rollout to production.
Track status under Test and release > Latest releases and bundles; allow at least a week between submitting and going live.
requirements.verify: Agent: edits.tracks.get for production shows the release 'completed'; the Play Console Publishing overview shows no pending changes and the store URL https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=<package> returns the listing.

requirements.title: Apple Developer Program membership active (US$99 per year), Apple Account with two-factor authentication
requirements.why: Membership is the prerequisite for App Store Connect; the legal name on the Apple Account becomes the seller name and an alias or company name in the Apple Account delays approval.
owner_steps: Open https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/ and click Start your enrollment (or use the Apple Developer app).
Sign in with an Apple Account that has two-factor authentication on and legal first and last names.

Individual: confirm legal name, email, phone and address (no PO boxes). Organization: have legal binding authority and a D-U-N-S number; your organization email/website must be public and functional (see as.duns-organization).
Agree to the Apple Developer Program License Agreement and pay US$99 (fee waivers exist for nonprofits, accredited educational institutions and government entities).
requirements.verify: Agent: an App Store Connect API call with the team's API key (for example GET https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com/v1/apps) returns 200.

requirements.title: Organization enrollment: D-U-N-S number and legal entity verification
requirements.why: Apple verifies identity, legal entity status and address through the nine-digit D-U-N-S number; DBAs, fictitious names, trade names and branches are not accepted and the website must be public and functional.
owner_steps: Look up or request a D-U-N-S number at https://developer.apple.com/support/D-U-N-S/.
During enrollment at https://developer.apple.com/programs/enroll/ enter the legal entity name, D-U-N-S, work email on the organization's domain, phone and a public website.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms enrollment status in the Apple Developer account. Not applicable for individual accounts.

requirements.title: Account Holder has accepted the latest agreements in App Store Connect Business
requirements.why: Apps cannot be created until the Account Holder signs the latest agreements; a new agreement version blocks creating apps until accepted.
owner_steps: Open https://appstoreconnect.apple.com and click Business at the top of the page.
On the Agreements tab, click View and Agree to Terms on any row that asks for acceptance, read and click Agree (two-factor code may be requested).
requirements.verify: Owner confirms Business > Agreements shows no pending agreement. Agent: app creation or an App Store Connect API write fails until accepted.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Paid Apps Agreement active with tax forms and bank account
requirements.applies_when: app is paid or sells In-App Purchases/subscriptions
requirements.why: Selling anything requires the Account Holder to sign the Paid Apps Agreement, then submit tax forms, then add a bank account; status must be Active. A free app with no IAP needs none of this.
owner_steps: Open https://appstoreconnect.apple.com, click Business, on the Agreements tab find the Paid Apps row and click View and Agree to Terms, read and click Agree (irreversible).
In the Tax Forms section click Add Tax Info next to the form you need (US developers complete a W-9; other regions have their own forms).
In the Bank Accounts section click Add Bank Account, choose the bank's country or region and fill the required fields.
Wait until the Paid Apps row shows Active.
requirements.verify: Agent: IAP/subscription products can be created and tested in sandbox only when the agreement is Active; the App Store Connect Business page row shows Active (owner confirms).
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change. Section was renamed Business (previously Agreements, Tax, and Banking).

requirements.title: EU Digital Services Act trader status declared (account level, plus per-app if trader)
requirements.why: Apple requires trader status to submit apps for the EU storefronts; traders must give address, phone, email and business documents which become public on the EU product page; non-traders are shown as not subject to EU consumer rights.
owner_steps: Open https://appstoreconnect.apple.com, select Business at the top, on the Agreements tab scroll to Compliance and next to Digital Services Act click Complete Compliance Requirements (Account Holder or Admin).

Choose 'This is a trader account.' or 'This is not a trader account.'; if trader, enter and confirm contact information, validate email and phone with two-factor codes, upload a current document verifying business name and address, then Next and Confirm.
Per app (traders): Apps > select app > General > App Compliance > Digital Services Act > Edit.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the Compliance section shows the DSA row complete. App Store Connect prompts for trader status at the next new-app submission if it is not declared.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change. Scope: Every developer declares; self-assessed trader or non-trader. No App Store Connect API endpoint for DSA trader status was found, so this stays an owner step.

requirements.title: Bundle ID registered and App Store Connect app record created
requirements.why: The app record is created before any build is uploaded; the bundle ID cannot change after a build is uploaded and the SKU cannot change after creation.
requirements.agent_path: Bundle IDs can be registered with the App Store Connect API (POST /v1/bundleIds, not re-read here); the Help page does not say the API can create the app record, so creation is a console action.
owner_steps: Register the bundle ID under Identifiers at https://developer.apple.com/account/resources/identifiers/list (Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles).
Open https://appstoreconnect.apple.com, go to Apps, click the + button at top left and choose New App.
Select platforms, enter App name, Primary language, Bundle ID, SKU and User Access (Full or Limited), then click Create (role: Account Holder, Admin or App Manager).
requirements.verify: Agent: GET /v1/apps?filter[bundleId]=<id> returns the app.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Build uploaded with Xcode 26+ and the iOS 26 SDK
requirements.why: Since 2026-04-28 uploads must be built with Xcode 26 or later using the 26-series SDKs.
requirements.agent_path: Check the build's Info.plist DTXcode / DTPlatformVersion / DTSDKName values in the IPA and the build record in App Store Connect API (GET /v1/builds).
requirements.verify: Agent: DTSDKName in the IPA Info.plist starts with iphoneos26 and App Store Connect accepts the upload without ITMS errors.

requirements.title: iOS/iPadOS minimum deployment target is iOS 13 or later
requirements.why: The Upcoming Requirements page lists 'iOS and iPadOS apps must target iOS 13 or later' dated 2026-09-09 under items that block submission or upload.
requirements.agent_path: Read MinimumOSVersion from the IPA Info.plist.
requirements.verify: Agent: MinimumOSVersion >= 13.0.
requirements.caveat: Quoted as the page states it; the practical floor of a modern game is far above 13.

requirements.title: Privacy manifest with approved reasons for required-reason APIs (including third-party SDKs)
requirements.why: Since 2024-05-01 approved reasons are required for required-reason APIs including those used by SDKs.
requirements.agent_path: Inspect PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in the app and every embedded framework; App Store Connect emails ITMS-91053 style issues after upload.
requirements.verify: Agent: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy present for the app and each SDK that needs one; upload processed with no required-reason warnings.

requirements.title: Build uploaded, processed, and attached to the version
requirements.why: Only one build can be associated with a version and it must be chosen before Submit for Review; a build in 'Missing Compliance' blocks submission until export-compliance questions are answered.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API: GET /v1/builds?filter[app]=<id>, then PATCH /v1/appStoreVersions/{id}/relationships/build; the repo's mobile-deploy-hub performs upload.
owner_steps: Console path: Apps > select the app > click the version in the sidebar > Build section > + > select the build > Done > Save (role: Account Holder, Admin or App Manager).
requirements.verify: Agent: the appStoreVersion's build relationship is set and the build processingState is VALID.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Export compliance answered for the build (ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption)
requirements.why: Apps using encryption must answer export questions per build or set the Info.plist key once; a 'Missing Compliance' build cannot be submitted. Documentation may be needed for non-exempt encryption (and France controls apply when distributing there).
requirements.agent_path: Set ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption in Info.plist at build time; App Store Connect API appEncryptionDeclarations resources exist.
owner_steps: If asked in console: Apps > app > version > Build > Manage next to the build and answer the encryption questions.
requirements.verify: Agent: the Info.plist key is present in the IPA and the build shows no 'Missing Compliance'.
requirements.caveat: The page does not name the Info.plist key; ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption comes from Apple's linked documentation and general knowledge.

requirements.title: App Privacy data-collection answers published
requirements.why: Apps must publish data-handling disclosures including third-party SDK collection; the product page cannot go live without it.
requirements.agent_path: No App Store Connect API endpoint for App Privacy data usages was found in the API documentation index read (app-metadata topics list app-infos, localizations, versions, screenshots, age-ratings, categories, accessibility-declarations only). Fastlane-style private endpoints exist but are unofficial.
owner_steps: Open https://appstoreconnect.apple.com, Apps > select the app > sidebar: App Privacy (role: Account Holder, Admin or App Manager).

Click Get Started; choose 'No, we do not collect data from this app' and Save, or choose Yes and select every data type collected by you and third-party partners, then answer the follow-ups for each type.
Review the Product Page Preview and click Publish (top right), confirming accuracy.
requirements.verify: Owner confirms the App Privacy page shows Published.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change. Scope: Even 'no data collected'. No App Store Connect API endpoint for App Privacy was found (only unofficial private endpoints), so this stays an owner step.

requirements.title: Privacy policy URL in App Store Connect and a link inside the app
requirements.why: A privacy policy URL is required for all iOS apps and Guideline 5.1.1(i) requires the link in the metadata and inside the app.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API: appInfoLocalizations privacyPolicyUrl (resource page exists in the API index); agent hosts and curl-checks the page.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > App Privacy > next to Privacy Policy click Edit, enter the URL (and optional Privacy Choices URL), Save.
requirements.verify: Agent: curl -sI <url> returns 200; the app has a reachable link; appInfoLocalizations shows the URL.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Age rating questionnaire answered (updated 2026 questions)
requirements.why: The age rating is a required app information property; unrated apps cannot be published. Apple asked developers to answer the updated questions by 2026-01-31 to avoid interrupted submissions.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API 'age-ratings' resources (ageRatingDeclarations) exist under Managing Categories and Age Declarations.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > sidebar General > App Information > Age Ratings > Set Up Age Ratings.

Select in-app controls and capabilities, choose a frequency for each content description, Next, then under 'Age Categories and Override' choose Not Applicable, Made for Kids or Override to Higher Age Rating; Save.
requirements.verify: Agent: the ageRatingDeclaration for the appInfo has no null questions; App Information shows a calculated rating.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Age-assurance obligations (Declared Age Range API etc.) for covered regions
requirements.applies_when: app rated 18+ or distributed in Brazil, Australia, Singapore, Utah or Louisiana (and Texas if enforced)
requirements.why: Apple blocks 18+ downloads in Australia, Brazil and Singapore for unconfirmed adults automatically; developers may have separate legal obligations. Apple states it does not block submission.
requirements.agent_path: Implement the Declared Age Range API (iOS 26+) if legal obligations apply.
requirements.verify: Agent: a documented decision per region; no App Review gate exists per the Apple news posts read.
requirements.caveat: Texas SB2420: Apple paused implementation after an injunction (2025-12-23 post), a search summary says the injunction was later lifted with a June 4, 2026 start; the Utah HB 498 deadline claim (2027-05-06) is unverified. Needs legal judgement, not a store gate.

requirements.title: Primary category and Content Rights declaration
requirements.why: Primary category and the content-rights answer (third-party content) are part of App Information; Games needs a subcategory choice of one or two.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API app-categories and app-infos resources.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > General > App Information > set Primary Category (and optional secondary/subcategories) and answer Content Rights.
requirements.verify: Agent: appInfo primaryCategory is set; content rights declared.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Price set (free is a price) and availability chosen
requirements.why: Pricing must be set before submitting for review; the Account Holder must have accepted the Paid Apps Agreement to offer anything but free.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API POST /v1/appPriceSchedules (base territory + price point) and app availability resources.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > sidebar Monetization > Pricing and Availability > Price Schedule > Add Pricing; select base country or region, choose a price, Next, review per-storefront prices, Next, then Confirm (role: Account Holder, Admin or App Manager).
requirements.verify: Agent: GET /v1/apps/{id}/appPriceSchedule returns a schedule; availability lists the intended territories.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Version metadata: description (4000), keywords (100 bytes), copyright, name (2-30), subtitle (30), promotional text (170)
requirements.why: Description, keywords, support URL and copyright are explicitly required for submission; name is 2-30 characters; What's New is required only from the second version.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API appStoreVersionLocalizations (description, keywords, whatsNew, supportUrl, promotionalText) and appInfoLocalizations (name, subtitle).
requirements.verify: Agent: all required localization fields non-empty and within limits for the primary language.
requirements.caveat: Required/optional column read from the page text; the separate Required-properties page lost its check marks in conversion, so the 'required' status of each field rests on the Platform version information page.

requirements.title: Support URL (and optional marketing URL) live and working
requirements.why: Support URL is required with full protocol; Guideline 2.1 rejects placeholder or dead URLs.
requirements.agent_path: Agent hosts the page and curl-verifies; set through appStoreVersionLocalizations supportUrl.
requirements.verify: Agent: curl -sI <support URL> returns 200 with real contact content.

requirements.title: Screenshots: iPhone 'Dynamic Island (medium)' 1179x2556 or 1206x2622, iPad 13in 2064x2752 or 2048x2732 if the app runs on iPad
requirements.why: At least one screenshot (up to ten) per required display size, JPEG/PNG with no alpha; other sizes scale from these.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API appScreenshotSets / appScreenshots (reserve, upload operations, then mark uploaded with checksum).
requirements.verify: Agent: appScreenshotSets for the required display types each have >=1 appScreenshot with state COMPLETE.
requirements.caveat: The page also states iPhone Duo screenshots become required from April 2027 for apps using the iOS 27.1 SDK or later (not applicable now). Scope: IPad set only if the app supports iPadOS.

requirements.title: 1024x1024 App Store icon in the app's asset catalog
requirements.why: Without the 1024x1024 PNG in the asset catalog the build is rejected at upload (ITMS-90704) and cannot be submitted.
requirements.agent_path: Inspect the Xcode asset catalog / export preset for the 1024 icon; upload validation fails otherwise.
requirements.verify: Agent: the IPA's AppIcon asset includes a 1024x1024 image without transparency issues; upload not rejected for missing icon.
requirements.caveat: Evidence is Apple Developer Forums and search results; Apple's Xcode doc 'configuring your app icon' was not fetched.

requirements.title: App Review information: contact name, email, phone (international format) and notes
requirements.why: Contact name, email and phone are required; notes are up to 4000 bytes.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API appStoreReviewDetails (contact fields, demoAccount fields, notes).
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > version > App Review Information section.
requirements.verify: Agent: appStoreReviewDetail has non-empty contactFirstName/LastName/Phone (+country code)/Email.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Demo account credentials (or demo mode) for App Review
requirements.why: Guideline 2.1 requires a working, non-expiring demo account with the backend live; credentials go in App Review information.
requirements.agent_path: Set demoAccountRequired and credentials via appStoreReviewDetails; agent keeps the demo account alive.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > version > App Review Information > Sign-in required: enter username and password; put extra accounts in Notes.
requirements.verify: Agent: logging in with the stored demo credentials works against production from a clean install.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable if the app has no sign-in.

requirements.title: App is a final, working version: no placeholders, working URLs, no crashes, IAPs complete (Guideline 2.1, 4.2)
requirements.why: Crashes, placeholder content, dead links or incomplete bundles lead to rejection; the app must be more than a repackaged website.
requirements.agent_path: Agent runs the release build on a device, checks links and crash-free launch (the game's own gates).
requirements.verify: Agent: release-build smoke test passes and all in-app URLs return 200.

requirements.title: In-app account deletion (Guideline 5.1.1(v)); revoke Sign in with Apple tokens
requirements.why: Any app that supports account creation must let users initiate deletion in the app, deleting the account record and personal data, available to everyone regardless of region.
requirements.agent_path: Agent builds the flow; use the Sign in with Apple REST API revoke-tokens endpoint when applicable.
requirements.verify: Agent: Settings has a discoverable delete-account action that completes deletion (or links directly to a web deletion page); deletion removes UGC and handles subscriptions.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to apps with no accounts.

requirements.title: Sign in with Apple or equivalent privacy-preserving login (Guideline 4.8)
requirements.applies_when: app uses a third-party or social login for the primary account
requirements.why: Third-party/social login for the primary account requires an equivalent login service that limits data to name and email, allows private email and avoids ad tracking without consent; exemptions apply for own-account-system-only, enterprise/education and similar.
requirements.agent_path: Agent implements the equivalent login.
requirements.verify: Agent: if only first-party accounts or Game Center are used, record the exemption; otherwise the build offers an equivalent login.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable when only the app's own account system is used.

requirements.title: Kids category rules (parental gates, no third-party analytics/ads, children's privacy laws)
requirements.applies_when: app marked Made for Kids or in the Kids Category
requirements.why: Made for Kids cannot be changed after approval and all updates must follow Guideline 1.3; Made for Kids is only available at calculated 4+ or 9+.
requirements.agent_path: Agent audits SDKs and links.
requirements.verify: Agent: not applicable unless Made for Kids is selected.

requirements.title: In-App Purchases configured, reviewable, restorable, and submitted with the version
requirements.applies_when: app sells digital goods or subscriptions
requirements.why: IAP must be complete, visible to the reviewer and functional; unlocks must use IAP with a restore mechanism; submission items can be added alongside the version.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API inAppPurchasesV2 and subscriptions resources; IAP review screenshot and metadata.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > Monetization > In-App Purchases; add each product with reference name, product ID, price, display name, description and App Review screenshot; add them to the draft submission via Add for Review.
requirements.verify: Agent: each product state is READY_TO_SUBMIT or approved; the app shows the products in a sandbox run.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable to a free app with no digital goods.

requirements.title: Game Center entitlement in the build and Game Center configured in App Store Connect
requirements.why: Apps using Game Center must have the entitlement and Game Center set up in App Store Connect; leaderboards/achievements submit with the version.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API gameCenterDetail resources.
requirements.verify: Agent: entitlement present in the signed IPA; GET /v1/apps/{id}/gameCenterDetail returns the config.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable if Game Center is not used.

requirements.title: App Tracking Transparency prompt and purpose strings
requirements.why: Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires explicit permission via ATT for tracking; apps may not require enabling system functions to use the app.
requirements.agent_path: Agent audits SDKs for tracking.
requirements.verify: Agent: no tracking SDK, or ATT prompt with purpose string present.
requirements.caveat: Not applicable if no tracking.

requirements.title: Region-specific licensing fields (Korea GRAC, China ICP, Vietnam game license, regulated medical devices)
requirements.applies_when: app distributed in Republic of Korea (org accounts), mainland China, Vietnam, or is a regulated medical-device/health app in EU/UK/US
requirements.why: App Information lists conditional compliance fields; they only block if the app is distributed there or meets the criteria.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > General > App Information; for the region you keep available, fill the Korea/China/Vietnam/medical-device fields shown; otherwise remove that region in Pricing and Availability.
requirements.verify: Agent: territories in availability exclude regions whose fields are unfilled.
requirements.caveat: Simplest compliance for a hobby game is to omit these regions.

requirements.title: Accessibility Nutrition Labels (not yet mandatory)
requirements.applies_when: voluntary as of 2026-11-20; Apple says it will become required for new apps and updates with ample notice
requirements.why: Apple states providing labels is voluntary now and will later be required for submissions; no date given.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API accessibility-declarations resources exist.
requirements.verify: Agent: re-check https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ each launch pass for a new date.
requirements.caveat: Mark not applicable with reason 'not yet mandatory' until Apple dates it.

requirements.title: Version release option chosen (manual, automatic, or automatic no earlier than a date)
requirements.why: Each platform version needs a release option; manual leaves the approved app in Pending Developer Release until you release it.
requirements.agent_path: appStoreVersions releaseType attribute via the App Store Connect API.
owner_steps: Console: Apps > app > version > App Store Version Release > pick 'Manually release this version', 'Automatically release this version' or the 'no earlier than' option, then Save (role: Account Holder, Admin or App Manager).
requirements.verify: Agent: appStoreVersion.releaseType is set.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.

requirements.title: Add for Review and Submit for Review
requirements.why: The version must be submitted to App Review (Add for Review, then Submit for Review); the API call is the equivalent of the Submit for Review button and errors on missing required info.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API review-submissions: create a reviewSubmission, add the appStoreVersion as a reviewSubmissionItem, then PATCH submitted=true (resource pages exist in the API index; the Help page links to the Version Submissions doc).
owner_steps: Open https://appstoreconnect.apple.com, Apps > select the app > click the version in the sidebar and verify the Build section.
Click Add for Review (top right), choose an existing draft submission or create a new one (status becomes Ready for Review).
Click Draft Submissions (bottom right) or App Review in the sidebar, open the submission and click Submit for Review (role: Account Holder, Admin or App Manager); status becomes In Review.
requirements.verify: Agent: GET /v1/apps/{id}/reviewSubmissions shows state WAITING_FOR_REVIEW/IN_REVIEW; the version status is Waiting for Review.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change. The review-submissions request shapes come from the API doc index plus general knowledge; the page body did not render. Confirm against a dry run before relying on them.

requirements.title: App approved and released to the App Store
requirements.why: Publication means Ready for Distribution; with manual release the owner must click Release This Version, and the app can take up to 24 hours to appear.
requirements.agent_path: App Store Connect API appStoreVersionReleaseRequests (manual release) per the Help page.
owner_steps: If the version status is Pending Developer Release: Apps > select the app > select that version in the sidebar > Release This Version (top right) > Confirm. Releases are per platform.
requirements.verify: Agent: appStoreVersionState is READY_FOR_SALE and https://apps.apple.com/app/id<appleId> loads the product page.
requirements.caveat: Menu path quoted from the cited App Store Connect Help page as read on 2026-11-20; App Store Connect menus change.
